summary: Service account impersonation blocked by IAM Condition after org-wide policy change
description:
Issue summary: After a recent org-wide IAM policy update, ephemeral CI runners started failing to start deploy jobs that require service account impersonation. The failing step is when the runner attempts to exchange the OIDC token for a short-lived Service Account (SA) credential using iamcredentials.generateAccessToken with an impersonation binding in place.

Impact: Blocked internal canary and hotfix deploys across multiple repos for the us-east prod region. Affects scheduled releases and ad-hoc deploys using the runner-provisioner flow. No externally visible customer outage, but internal release velocity is impaired.

Environment: prod | us-east. CI fleet: self-hosted GitHub Actions runners managed by runner-provisioner service. Affected SA: ci-deployer@redwood-prod.

Observed behavior: Runners fail with 403 "Request had insufficient authentication scopes" when calling IAM Credentials API to impersonate ci-deployer. Attempts to fallback to alternate SA fail due to policy scope.

Initial hypothesis: A recently applied IAM Condition on the org folder-level binding tightened who can impersonate specific SAs; runners' OIDC claims no longer satisfy the condition. Possible root causes: newer "requireXpn" style condition, missing attribute in OIDC token, or misapplied group predicate in the condition.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger a deploy workflow that uses runner-provisioner to create ephemeral runner and impersonate ci-deployer SA.
2) Observe runner start logs until the impersonation step.
3) See immediate failure on step that exchanges OIDC token for SA access token (iamcredentials.generateAccessToken) with 403 error.
4) Attempt to manually call IAM Credentials API from a token with same OIDC claims and receive same 403 response.
logs: 2026-03-10T09:14:03Z runner-1234 provisioner: attempting SA impersonation for ci-deployer@redwood-prod

2026-03-10T09:14:03Z iamcredentials: generateAccessToken failed: PERMISSION_DENIED: Request had insufficient authentication scopes.
    resource=projects/-/serviceAccounts/ci-deployer@redwood-prod
2026-03-10T09:16:21Z gcp-iam: evaluated condition expr 'request.auth.claims.email == "deploy-bot@redwood.com"' -> false (runner OIDC claim: service_account_identity=ci-runner-ephemeral)
2026-03-10T09:22:10Z runner-1234: fallback SA attempt also denied: PERMISSION_DENIED
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 10:00 - Diego M: Confirmed 403s originate from IAM Conditions block using policy simulator; condition expression requires explicit 'email' claim which ephemeral runners do not present.
2026-03-10 11:10 - Diego M: Cross-checked OIDC issuer claims from runners: we emit 'service_account_identity' and 'instance_id', not 'email'.

2026-03-10 13:05 - SRE on-call (Rae Chen): Verified recent change: Org Policy 'restrict-service-account-impersonation' applied 2026-03-09 23:40 UTC by infra-admin. Condition added requiring request.auth.claims.email == 'deploy-bot@redwood.com' or member in group://infra-deployers@redwood.com.
2026-03-11 09:30 - Security (M. Alvarez): Confirmed org-level change was intentional to lock down human SA impersonation vectors; however it unintentionally matched for runner flows.
2026-03-11 11:20 - Diego M: Reproduced manual token call with patched OIDC token including 'email' claim — impersonation succeeds. Shows token claim difference is root cause.

2026-03-12 08:45 - Diego M: Prepared mitigation plan: (1) temporary allowlist on condition for runner identity 'service_account_identity' values, (2) longer-term: update runner OIDC token provider to emit required claim or update condition to check group membership via 'request.auth.claims.kubernetes_service_account' if available.
comments: Aisha Kapoor (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Noticed multiple deploy pipelines failing around 09:14 UTC. Pinging SRE and Infra for help — this is blocking our Friday hotfix window.
Diego Martinez (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Investigating. Initial check suggests IAM Condition is denying impersonation. Will correlate with recent org policy changes.
Rae Chen (SRE) 2026-03-10: Confirmed the policy change. Will open an infra-ops escalation to get temporary exception if possible.
Marco Alvarez (Security) 2026-03-11: Security approved a narrow temporary exception for runner identities while we implement a permanent fix. Exception must be time-limited and logged.
Diego Martinez 2026-03-12: Applying temporary exception now: added runner identity predicate to the condition for 72 hours. Requesting release team to retry blocked deploys.
Release Manager (Olivia Park) 2026-03-12: Hotfix deploy succeeded after exception applied. Please proceed with follow-ups to avoid recurrence.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation: added a targeted predicate to the org IAM Condition to allow the runner identity 'service_account_identity' values to impersonate ci-deployer for 72 hours. Permanent fix options agreed: (A) update runner OIDC token provider to include 'email' claim matching allowed identity, or (B) update org IAM Condition to evaluate a stable runner claim (service_account_identity or k8s SA) and/or group membership.

Current status: Mitigation applied and verified; blocked deploys resumed. Working on implementation plan for option B (less invasive to runner token generation).
follow_up_actions: 1) Diego M - Implement change to IAM Condition to use 'service_account_identity' predicate and test in staging (due 2026-03-18).
2) Runner team - Investigate adding stable 'email' or group claim to OIDC tokens emitted to GCP (due 2026-03-25).
3) Security - Review and sign-off updated condition and document exception window and audit logs (due 2026-03-20).
4) Ops - Add monitoring alert for impersonation 403 spike to #infra-alerts (done: action item to tune thresholds).
